business_problem: Exscientia wanted to shrink the time, cost, and failure rate of drug discovery, where conventional methods can take up to 15 years, cost over 2 billion dollars, and still fail 90–96 percent of the time.
solution_summary: Exscientia built a design-make-test-learn platform on AWS that combines generative AI, active learning, and robotic lab automation to accelerate drug discovery. The company starts with target product profiles, then uses algorithms trained on public pharmacology data plus proprietary patient tissue samples, genomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and medical literature to generate candidate compounds in the cloud. Active learning narrows those candidates to the most promising molecules, and automated robots synthesize and test them in a lab orchestrated by AWS microservices. The resulting experimental data feeds back into future DMTL cycles so Exscientia can improve predictions, reduce the number of compounds it has to make, and move candidates to the clinic faster.

solution_components.name: AWS microservices
solution_components.role: Orchestrate the automated robotic lab that closes the design-make-test-learn loop.

data_flow: Public pharmacology data, patient tissue samples, genomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and medical literature train Exscientia’s generative models; active learning narrows the candidate list, robots synthesize and test compounds, and the resulting data feeds future design-make-test-learn cycles.
business_outcome: Exscientia makes 10 times fewer compounds than the industry average, has accelerated drug design by up to 70 percent, decreased capital cost by 80 percent, and has already advanced six AI-designed molecules into clinical trials.
